title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Commercial and office cleaning
audience: Owners and account managers of commercial and office cleaning businesses who quote contract, recurring and one-off office work.
learningOutcomes: Write an office-cleaning offer with a clear promised standard, visit window, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk a facilities manager or landlord carries, and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only on time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'We clean offices' is a service. 'We clean each floor, the kitchens, the amenities and the high-touch surfaces every weeknight to a written checklist, leave a signed sign-off sheet on each floor, and re-clean any item the building manager flags at the next nightly visit' is an offer. The facilities manager buys a standard they can check and a supplier they will not have to chase.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: A clear outcome, such as amenities and kitchens ready for staff by 7 am; a defined visit window agreed with the building; the work the client must do, such as after-hours access and bin locations; the certainty you provide, such as a checklist, sign-off sheets and a monthly audit; and the risk you carry, such as the re-clean promise. Keep each part specific and checkable. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, because a written quote can become binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', last updated 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Make after-hours access, key or swipe-card handling and the sign-off step simple. One named contact at the building and one monthly report reduce the decisions a facilities manager has to make. Clients often accept a higher price for fewer interruptions, because they are paying for reliability.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to services, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services. A written workmanship warranty is an optional extra that sits on top of those guarantees (business.gov.au, 'Warranties and refunds', last updated 27 May 2025). Consumer Victoria explains that a service provider gets a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (last updated 13 October 2023), but that page sets no fix window, so write your own. Do not publish a measured claim, such as a percentage of surfaces passing a test, unless you can show the test. Check current ACCC guidance before publishing any measurable claim.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the outcome and the risk, then check against your cost and visit time. Vendor guidance gives $35 to $65 per hour for most office and business premises, and $140 to $180 per visit for a 300 m² Sydney office on a basic scope at three visits a week (Clean Group, updated 15 March 2026). That is a sales source for one city, so use it as a check, not a target. List optional extras, such as a quarterly carpet extraction, as separate lines beside the base price (Business Queensland, last updated 16 November 2022). Stepped packages, with each higher tier adding something the facilities manager can see, are one way to present the offer (Jobber Academy, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024). A study of an AI assistant's three-plan offers, which was not a cleaning business, found that reversing the plan order raised revenue by 10.8 per cent (INSEAD Knowledge, 2 October 2025), so test the order in your own tenders. Show one clear total and say whether GST is included (ACCC, last modified 15 July 2026).

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a facilities manager would repeat.
Set a visit window you have checked against the building's access rules and your crew's past nights, and record how often you meet it.
List what the client must do, such as access, bins and consumables if agreed, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: a floor-by-floor checklist with a sign-off sheet or photos.
Decide the re-clean promise and check that you can staff it within the time you state.
Price from value, then check the per-visit or monthly price against your cost per hour and the vendor ranges.

workedExamples.situation: An owner quotes an hourly rate for an office clean and loses tenders to suppliers that offer a fixed monthly price. Facilities managers say they cannot compare the hourly quotes with the others.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer as a monthly price and check it against your cost and the vendor range.
workedExamples.reasoning: A monthly price for a stated checklist, visit window, sign-off process and re-clean promise lets the facilities manager compare like with like. The vendor's basic-scope figures for a 300 m² Sydney office are $140 to $180 per visit at three visits a week, which is $1,680 to $2,160 a month across 12 visits (Clean Group, updated 15 March 2026). That is a Sydney reference, not a rule for your area. Set your own price from your cost per visit, then check it against the range, and write the visit count into the offer, because the monthly figure depends on it.

commonErrors.error: Making a re-clean promise you cannot staff
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the promise to a re-clean within a time you can staff, and write it into the offer.

commonErrors.error: Quoting a monthly price with no visit count or scope
commonErrors.prevention: State the visits per month, the scope and the exclusions. The vendor's monthly figures change with the visit count, for example 12 visits for three evenings a week and 20 for five (Clean Group, updated 15 March 2026).

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. The Australian Consumer Law applies nationally, but state and territory fair trading rules differ, so check the rules for each state where you work. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority.

qualityStandard: Every commercial offer states the standard, visit window, client inputs, re-clean promise and GST status, and is checked against cost and visit time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer with scope, standard, exclusions and visit window, the price basis, and the decision made.
summary: A commercial offer promises a checkable standard, a visit window, certainty and a re-clean promise you can afford.
Higher rates follow from a clearer standard and lower risk for the facilities manager, not from longer hours.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of an office-cleaning offer does the facilities manager buy?
options: The standard and certainty of getting it

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a re-clean promise be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new clients and friends
Something you can staff, afford and deliver within a stated time

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a measurable claim, such as a percentage of surfaces passing a test, have?

officialReferences.title: Setting prices: what's allowed (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: Taken from the research file (team4-R-sol03-tactics, tactic 11): misleading statements about price are prohibited, which supports showing one all-in price with GST status. The page was not re-read for this variant. Whether it covers minimum or call-out charges is not confirmed. Publisher: ACCC.

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. Supports: a written quote becomes binding once accepted.

business.gov.au, 'Warranties and refunds', https://www.business.gov.au/Products-and-services/Fair-trading/Warranties-and-refunds, last updated 27 May 2025. Supports: an optional warranty sits on top of consumer guarantees; a 'no refunds' line does not override rights for services.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Supports: a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge. The page sets no fix-window length.

Clean Group, 'Commercial cleaning pricing guide', https://www.clean-group.com.au/how-much-does-workplace-cleaning-cost-in-australia, updated 15 March 2026. Vendor source. Supports: per-hour range for office premises; per-visit range for a 300 m² Sydney office; monthly figures by visit count.

Business Queensland, 'Preparing a business quote: tips', https://www.business.qld.gov.au/running-business/marketing-sales/sales/preparing-quote/tips, last updated 16 November 2022. Supports: optional extras shown as separate lines on the quote.

Jobber Academy, 'Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples', https://getjobber.com/academy/good-better-best-pricing-examples/, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024. Older source; supports stepped packages.

INSEAD Knowledge, 'Small Change, Big Rewards', https://knowledge.insead.edu/marketing/small-change-big-rewards, 2 October 2025. Supports: reversing plan order raised revenue by 10.8 per cent in one experiment. Not a trade study.
